newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 28.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on its front page on July 28:

WASHINGTON - Congressional Republicans, eager to conclude a budget agreement, signaled they are ready to make major concessions to the White House on a proposed $500-per-child family tax credit and a reduction in the capital gains tax.
WASHINGTON - Congress is on the verge of reducing the government's tax bite on estates left by wealthy people when they die.
WASHINGTON - Misunderstandings and deceptions jumbled to force out House Speaker Newt Gingrich in a recent aborted coup.
STAFFORD, VIRGINIA - A 2-year old boy was found alive and well Sunday a day and a half after he wandered away from his home.
WASHINGTON - Despite a few opening day jitters, operations ran smoothly at the new National Airport terminal.

WASHINGTON - In workplaces across the country, helping employees balance job and family has become a hot topic, but a Washington Post survey found that some organizations that call themselves pro-family are doing only the minimum required by law.
